phase: P8: Android on a real phone
device: Samsung Galaxy A12 (SM-A125F), Android 12 (API 31), arm64-v8a, 720x1600 at 300 dpi, 2.8 GB RAM (MemTotal 2809044 kB), connected by the user over USB
install: the debug APK installs (adb install, 221 MB); the first launch extracts the game data
finding 1: screen: first vs run: boundary OriginalMacDisplayBackend.Boundary.geometry at the first front-screen blit (iteration 5): the host told the game a 853x384 dp screen, so the centred 794x550 window started at y=-83 and the blit's rectangle was partly above the screen. Fix: the Android host reports the surface in dp scaled up (same aspect) to at least 800x600, the desktop the original was made for (this phone: 1333x600; the 1280x800 tablet emulator unchanged)
finding 2: memory: second run: no boundary; the game reached 'started' and its startup loading, then Android's low-memory killer ended it (lmkd: 'Reclaim local.ntsd.port ... to free 1311324kB rss, 2493324kB swap; reason: device is low on swap (0kB < 786428kB) and thrashing (272%)', then signal 9). Resident memory sampled every 4 s rose to 1.3 GB while available memory fell to ~50 MB
macOS comparison: the same vs scenario in the macOS headless build: maximum resident 1,715,961,856 bytes, peak memory footprint 4,165,046,040 bytes (/usr/bin/time -l): the game currently needs about 4 GB everywhere, more than this phone has
regression: emulator (tablet) with the new APK: vs equal; text in the same 446 of 1,826 frames as AppKit
open: the game's memory footprint (~4 GB) on phones with 3 GB of RAM: needs a memory-reduction study (e.g. memory-mapping the read-only game data, releasing startup inputs once loaded)
a phone with 6 GB or more
